notes:
Mid-market SaaS (revenue ops + SDR automation) — product team evaluating Redwood for outbound chat agents that can take actions (CRM update, send follow-up email, create calendar invite). Currently prototyping with a homegrown small LLM stack; primary concerns: consistent low-latency streaming, reliable tool-calling latency, and predictable monthly cost. Wants Hosted first for speed of test, then Dedicated if latency and SLOs hold. Head of Product: "If streaming is jerky it's a non‑starter — SDRs need near real-time typing and instant action confirmations." CEO cares about data separation and audit logs. Interested in built-in function/tool calling vs custom glue.

Ask: demo streaming + tool-calling flow (CRM write + email send) end-to-end. Need E2E latency targets: UI streaming token latency <100‑150ms, tool call roundtrip <200ms ideally. Will validate with synthetic load and real SDR sessions (25 concurrent agents).

use_case_summary: Primary workload: sales outbound chat assistant for SDRs. Must support streaming responses for typing indicator + immediate UI feedback, and function/tool calling to perform CRM updates, send templated emails, and schedule calendar events. Expected concurrency: 20-30 active SDR clients with peaks of 50. QPS low per-agent but strict P95 latency targets. Cost-sensitive but will pay for Dedicated if SLA guarantees latency and isolation. Prefer model routing to cheaper variants during non-peak.
